requirement: On deployment the admin holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE only; no supply exists, nothing is paused, and every role is administered by the default admin.
Only MINTER_ROLE can mint and burn.
Only PAUSER_ROLE can pause and unpause.
Only ALLOWLIST_ROLE can change the allowlist, and only DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can grant or revoke roles: governance and compliance are separate duties.
Every balance movement requires the sender, the recipient and, for transferFrom, the spender to be allowlisted; transferFrom is no bypass.
Revoking a role or delisting an account takes effect immediately (the very next call).
Pause stops every balance movement (transfer, transferFrom, mint, burn); admin and allowlist functions keep working.
Escrow is wired to its token, arbiter and admin at deployment, and refuses a zero token, arbiter or admin.
open pulls exactly the amount from the payer into escrow, records every field, assigns sequential ids and emits Opened.
open rejects a zero amount, an unpayable payee and a deadline that is not in the future (ESC-D4, ESC-D6).
Only the arbiter can release a Funded deal; release pays the payee the full amount, marks it Released and emits Released, also after the deadline.
From the deadline second on, anyone can refund a Funded deal, and the money always goes to the payer, never to the caller (ESC-D1, ESC-D2).
A deal settles once: Released and Refunded are terminal; any second release or refund reverts.
An id that was never opened can be neither released nor refunded.
The escrow defers to the token's allowlist: an unlisted escrow or payer cannot open, a delisted escrow stops payouts, and funds for a delisted payee are recoverable by refund.
While the token is paused, open, release and refund all revert; after unpause they succeed with funds intact.
For any valid amount and deadline, open records exactly that amount and deadline.
For any amount, open then release moves exactly that amount from payer to payee.
No address other than the arbiter can release, whatever it is.
No caller can refund at any second before the deadline.
A transfer conserves totalSupply and moves exactly the amount between the two parties.
No address without the matching role can mint, pause or change the allowlist.
Invariant: the escrow's token balance equals the sum of all Funded deals.
Invariant: payees received exactly what was released, and payers got back exactly what was refunded.
Invariant: tracked balances always sum to totalSupply; no value appears outside mint.
Invariant: a settled deal never changes state again.
Against real mainnet USDC (fork), escrow moves amounts exactly: 1 base unit, six-decimal amounts and amounts above 2^64.
Against real USDC, Circle's blacklist is respected: a blacklisted payer, payee or escrow blocks the affected flows with USDC's own revert.
The planted re-entrancy in VulnerableVault is exploitable: an attacker drains more than its stake (proves the exploit test can see the bug).
The checks-effects-interactions fix stops the re-entrancy.
The nonReentrant fix stops the re-entrancy, even with the vulnerable call order kept.
Both fixed vaults still serve honest withdrawals.
Admin renounce or handover can never happen by accident: it needs a scheduled two-step transfer after a two-day delay (issue #3).
An admin handover moves power only when the new admin accepts after the delay, not before and not at the exact schedule second.
Only the escrow admin can rotate the arbiter, never to the zero address, and rotation emits ArbiterChanged.
After rotation the old arbiter can no longer release, directly or with old signatures (F-07).
Rotation doesn't disturb in-flight deals, and the escrow admin cannot release deals itself.
A release signed by the arbiter can be submitted by anyone and pays the payee.
The same signed release cannot be submitted twice (nonce consumed).
A signature from another chain, or made before a chain-id change, is rejected (EIP-712 domain).
A signature made for another escrow contract is rejected.
An expired signature is rejected, and a submitter cannot change the signed deadline.
A signature for one deal cannot be reused for another.
Signatures from a non-arbiter, a rotated-out arbiter or a malleated (high-s) signature are rejected.
What is deployed is what forge built: runtime code matches the artifact, and the escrow is wired to the token and arbiter.
Over JSON-RPC, open moves exactly the amount, records the deal and emits Opened and Transfer from the right contracts.
Over JSON-RPC, the arbiter's release pays the payee in full and marks the deal Released.
Over JSON-RPC, a refund at the deadline pays the payer, never the caller.
Custom errors are decoded from revert data and asserted by name and arguments, including errors bubbled from the token through the escrow.
An EIP-712 release signed in Python verifies on chain, can be relayed by a third account, and cannot be replayed.
The EIP-712 typehash and domain separator computed in Python match the contract's.
Deadline boundaries hold to the exact second on a real node (deadline - 1 refused, deadline accepted).
A reverted transaction is distinguished from an included one: status 0 receipts are detected and decoded (F-13).
Concurrent sends from one account get distinct nonces and all land; a naive nonce strategy loses transfers (F-11).
Per-test evm_snapshot/evm_revert restores balances, deals and account nonces.
After a reorg (snapshot/revert), the indexer drops the abandoned block's events and indexes the replacement; the naive indexer must fail (F-15).
A same-height reorg (anvil_reorg) with no new block is detected by the tip check, also below a confirmation depth (F-18).
The naive indexer's failure is pinned: it keeps the abandoned transfer and misses the replacement.
A restart mid-sync loses no event and duplicates none; re-syncing with no new blocks changes nothing.
A crash inside a block's transaction commits nothing of that block, and the restart stores its events exactly once.
Events in one block are stored and replayed in log_index order, across contracts.
Amounts are exact integers end to end, up to 2^256 - 1; SQLite NUMERIC is never used for them (F-16).
A reorg shallower than the confirmation depth never reaches the database.
A reorg below the start block stops the indexer loudly instead of rebuilding from a guess.
Every holder's balanceOf at a pinned block hash equals the indexed balance.
The sum of indexed balances, and minted minus burned, both equal totalSupply.
The escrow's balance equals the sum of deals the database says are Funded.
Reconciliation is pinned to a confirmed block hash, so activity after the pin doesn't disturb it.
Reconciliation detects a one-unit discrepancy, per holder, even when totals still agree.
After a reorg the naive indexer fails reconciliation and the real one passes.
A transfer moves accepted, signed, submitted, mined, confirmed, one step per worker pass, and nothing moves at accept.
A transfer that reverts after being accepted is reported failed with the decoded error; no tokens move.
A request that would revert now is refused with 422 and the decoded error; nothing is stored and the key stays free.
Malformed requests are 422: amounts are decimal strings of base units (no JSON numbers), within 1..2^256-1; 2^53+1 round-trips exactly.
Replaying a request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same transfer; it is paid once.
Reusing an Idempotency-Key for a different request is 409 and creates nothing.
Ten concurrent requests with one key create one transfer and one payment (one 202, nine 200).
Ten concurrent distinct requests all confirm with consecutive nonces, and the payee receives the exact sum.
A transaction stuck after a fee spike (dropped by the node) is replaced at the same nonce and confirmed once (F-20).
After a crash between signing and broadcast, the restart sends the stored signed bytes exactly once.
After a crash between broadcast and recording it, the restart recognises its own transaction and pays once; re-signing would pay twice (F-21).
A server restart keeps accepted transfers; replays find them and the new worker sends them once.
A refused send cannot stall later transactions: the nonce manager re-syncs (issue #12, F-19).
A send from the hot wallet's key outside the service is recovered by re-sync and retry.
A send refused mid-tick leaves no nonce gap when the manager re-syncs.
A nonce lost without any error is filled with a 0-value self-transfer, so the transfers behind it execute.
When the backlog is full the API answers 503 + Retry-After and stores nothing; the same key succeeds later and pays once.
Each worker tick submits a bounded batch, so tracking and confirmations are never starved (F-23).
Under concurrent load all four user types (API read/write, RPC read/write) are served without request failures.
After load and drain, every accepted transfer is confirmed and the API's confirmed total equals what the hot wallet paid on chain.
Under load the indexer stays within 3 blocks of the head and reconciles with the chain afterwards.
Connecting a wallet shows the account and its exact balance.
A transfer is simulated, signed once, mined and reported as confirmed; balances move by exactly the amount.
A wallet rejection (4001) reports that nothing was sent; no transaction exists, balances are unchanged and the form keeps its values.
Amounts at or above the large-value threshold need a second confirmation showing the exact amount and recipient; the exact base units are sent (2^53+1).
Invalid amounts and recipients are refused with specific messages before the wallet is asked.
A transfer that would revert is explained and never signed; one that reverts after simulation is shown as failed on chain, never confirmed.
On the wrong network the page refuses to offer a transfer.
A double click or two same-tick submissions produce exactly one transaction (F-27).
The page's function and error selectors match the compiled contract.
Amounts round-trip exactly through the page's BigInt parsing and formatting, up to 2^256 - 1.
A failed UI test leaves a Playwright trace with the page's actions and DOM snapshots.
